intro.title: Relationship Depth Assessment
intro.body: Check your real dynamics — communication, resilience, personal space, and shared growth. Choose a quick check or full depth. Everything stays in your browser.

result.caption: Honest relationship profile
result.shareText: Our relationship profile: {{profile}} ({{score}}%). {{insight}} | Relationship Depth — DailyLogic

profiles.steady-partners: Steady partners — with room for gentle upgrades
profiles.quiet-strength: Quiet strength built from ordinary days
profiles.work-in-progress-good: Work in progress — the good kind
profiles.repair-ready: Ready to repair, not just dramatize
profiles.needs-attention: The system is asking for attention

insights.dim-resilience-high: Your resilience shows: under pressure there’s a base of “we’re in this together.” Keep that alive in quiet seasons too.
insights.dim-resilience-low: Resilience wants reinforcement — not heroics, but small reliability: who handles what when it’s hard.
insights.dim-communication-high: Your communication breathes. That’s rare — use it for boring topics, not only crises.
insights.dim-communication-low: There’s a gap between what’s felt and what’s said. Start with short, clean sentences — no prosecutions.
insights.dim-personalSpace-high: Personal space doesn’t threaten your bond — it feeds it. That’s relational maturity.
insights.dim-personalSpace-low: Togetherness may be crowding you. Space isn’t distance; it’s oxygen for the long run.
insights.dim-sharedGrowth-high: You have a shared direction. Even if the pace differs — there’s a compass.
insights.dim-sharedGrowth-low: Shared growth needs a tiny ritual: one goal, one talk, one celebration a month.
insights.overall-strong: The overall picture is strong and connected — without pretending everything is perfect.
insights.overall-steady: You’re in human steadiness: clear strengths and points that need maintenance.
insights.overall-developing: Real potential, with root-level work still ahead — not just a photo for social media.
insights.overall-needs-care: This report asks for gentleness and honesty: don’t blame; do pick one small action this week.
insights.balance-note: Healthy partnership isn’t perfect symmetry — it’s the ability to repair when balance slips.
insights.humor-note: If you can still laugh at yourselves sometimes — you have a repair tool apps can’t measure.

tips.tip-repair-ritual: Set a repair ritual after conflict: 10 minutes, no phones — what hurt, what you need.
tips.tip-stress-plan: Write ahead who does what under stress (kids, money, health). A plan lowers drama.
tips.tip-small-reliability: Pick one small weekly commitment and keep it — reliability builds resilience.
tips.tip-weekly-talk: A 20-minute weekly status: what worked, what hurts, what you’re asking for.
tips.tip-reflect-before-reply: Before a sharp reply — one breath and one clarifying question.
tips.tip-soft-start: Start hard sentences with “I feel” instead of “you always.”
tips.tip-alone-calendar: Block alone time for each person on the calendar — like a meeting you don’t cancel.
tips.tip-friend-night: A separate friends night every two weeks, without unnecessary mood checks.
tips.tip-no-scorekeeping: Stop scorekeeping who yielded more. Ask: what do I need right now?
tips.tip-shared-goal: Pick one small shared monthly goal (trip, savings, habit) and review together.
tips.tip-celebrate-tiny: Celebrate tiny wins out loud — ending a fight peacefully counts.
tips.tip-fair-chores: Rebalance home load monthly. Fairness updates; it isn’t locked forever.
tips.tip-common-sense-pause: When the volume rises — a 20-minute pause isn’t escape; it’s maintenance.

talk-hard-topics.prompt: When a sensitive topic comes up (money, family, future) — we can talk without fleeing or exploding.

options.1: Sensitive topics stay locked away — someone walks out, goes silent, or blows up
options.2: We start hard talks and shut down with "not now" or blame
options.3: We touch hard topics sometimes, but tiptoe or cut them short
options.4: We can open a tough conversation and stay in the room when it's uncomfortable
options.5: Money, family, and future get discussed openly — without fleeing or exploding

listen-to-understand.prompt: When my partner speaks — I listen to understand, not only to reply.

options.1: While my partner talks, I'm already building my reply or interrupting
options.2: I hear the words but rarely check what's underneath them
options.3: I listen okay, but slack off when I'm tired or stressed
options.4: I usually pause, ask one question, and reflect back before responding
options.5: I listen to understand your side — even when I disagree

repair-after-fight.prompt: After a fight, we know how to come back and repair — even if it takes time.

options.1: After a fight, the bad air stays — nobody comes back to repair
options.2: We wait for time to pass with no clear move toward connection
options.3: Someone says "let's make up" but the real issue stays open
options.4: We know how to return, apologize, or clarify — even if not the same day
options.5: We have a familiar repair path — words, touch, or talk that rebuilds trust

daily-checkins.prompt: We have small daily check-ins, not only an automatic “how was your day.”

options.1: Most days are a hallway "how's it going" and nothing more
options.2: We coordinate logistics without touching how we really feel
options.3: Now and then we get a short "how are you, actually"
options.4: We keep a small daily habit — coffee, a text, a hug before sleep
options.5: Every day we have a real touchpoint: how you are, what hurts, what you need

honest-without-cruel.prompt: We can be honest without humiliating, and tender without hiding.

options.1: Truth comes out as a weapon — or we hide everything to avoid hurt
options.2: Honesty lands sharp; tenderness gets left behind
options.3: We try to balance, but slip into sarcasm or silence
options.4: Hard things can be said in a tone that respects the person in front of me
options.5: We're honest and gentle together — truth without humiliation or hiding

disagree-respect.prompt: We can disagree without turning it into a loyalty test.

options.1: Disagreement quickly becomes "if you loved me you would..."
options.2: Someone raises their voice or shuts down — as if arguing equals betrayal
options.3: We can disagree, but it sometimes ends in digs or payback
options.4: Different views stay on the topic — not on our worth as a couple
options.5: We can think differently and still feel safe — no loyalty tests

humor-in-friction.prompt: Even in friction, we sometimes use healthy humor that cools heat without erasing pain.

options.1: Under tension, humor turns to mockery or we avoid talking entirely
options.2: We laugh to escape the issue — and it lands as dismissive
options.3: Sometimes a smile helps; sometimes it steamrolls the hurt
options.4: We can laugh together without canceling what's painful
options.5: We have light humor that cools heat — without belittling feelings

say-needs-clearly.prompt: I can ask for what I need instead of hinting and getting angry later.

options.1: I expect my partner to know what I need without me saying it
options.2: I hint, get angry, and we fight about "why didn't you get it"
options.3: Sometimes I'm direct; sometimes I fall back into hints
options.4: I usually ask clearly: "I need you to..."
options.5: I say what I need in plain words — no guessing games

crisis-support.prompt: In a crisis (health, work, family) — we feel we have each other’s back.

options.1: In crisis we each carry the stress alone
options.2: There's practical help, but it's hard to feel someone is truly with me
options.3: We show up when pushed, but don't always know how to be emotionally present
options.4: In hard times one of us holds the other — nights, calls, showing up
options.5: In health, work, or family crises — we know we have each other's back

stress-teamwork.prompt: Under stress we act more like a team than two tired opponents.

options.1: Under stress we fight about who's more exhausted
options.2: We each pull our own way — without coordinating
options.3: Sometimes we split tasks; sometimes we forget we're on the same side
options.4: We agree who takes what and remind ourselves we're a team
options.5: Under pressure we share the load and boost each other — not compete

bounce-after-hurt.prompt: When hurt happens — there’s a path back to trust, not only long silence.

options.1: When it hurts, long silence follows with no way back
options.2: We wait for time to heal without talking about what happened
options.3: We talk eventually, but trusting again feels shaky
options.4: We can open a conversation about the hurt and rebuild slowly
options.5: We have a clear path from pain back to trust — even when it takes time

money-tension.prompt: Money tension opens into conversation with us, not only suspicion.

options.1: Money means fights or secrets — not real conversation
options.2: One person controls the books; the other feels shut out or suspected
options.3: We talk when there's a crisis, not before
options.4: We have regular talks about budget and fears around money
options.5: Money tension opens in transparency — without suspicion or hidden control

family-pressure.prompt: Pressure from families of origin is handled as a couple, not a loyalty war.

options.1: Family pressure turns us into soldiers in a loyalty war
options.2: Each of us defends our parents — the couple gets sidelined
options.3: We try to align, but boundaries with family stay fuzzy
options.4: We talk as a couple first and go out with a shared line
options.5: Pressure from families of origin is handled together — clear boundaries, united

health-or-hard-week.prompt: In a hard week we adjust expectations instead of demanding “business as usual.”

options.1: In a hard week we still expect "business as usual"
options.2: One person crashes; the other gets upset they didn't "hold it together"
options.3: We dial expectations down a bit, without naming it
options.4: We adjust the routine — who covers what, and what can wait
options.5: In illness or exhaustion we reset expectations and care for each other on purpose

trust-under-doubt.prompt: Even when doubt appears — there’s a base of trust we can return to.

options.1: A little doubt topples everything — nothing to return to
options.2: When suspicion rises, chasing or punishing silence starts
options.3: There's basic trust, but doubts stay unaddressed
options.4: When something feels off, we talk instead of guessing
options.5: Even when doubt appears — there's trust we can return to in conversation

apologize-and-change.prompt: An apology with us comes with an attempt to change, not only pretty words.

options.1: "Sorry" comes fast — with no real change after
options.2: We apologize to end the fight, not to shift the pattern
options.3: There's apology and effort, but the same mistakes repeat
options.4: After sorry comes a concrete step: what we'll do differently
options.5: Apology comes with real change — not just pretty words

alone-time-ok.prompt: Alone time is accepted without offense or suspicion.

options.1: Time alone feels like abandonment or suspicion
options.2: Solo time is allowed, but with guilt or check-in texts
options.3: Sometimes it's fine; sometimes someone feels hurt we "disappeared"
options.4: We each have agreed alone time — without defending it every time
options.5: Personal time is welcome without hurt or suspicion — we come back connected

friends-without-guilt.prompt: We can see friends separately without a tiny sense of betrayal.

options.1: A night with friends sounds like a small betrayal
options.2: We go out, but with moody texts or a fight after
options.3: Mostly okay — with flashes of jealousy or guilt
options.4: We have separate friend nights — without policing each other
options.5: Each of us sees friends without guilt — and returns without loyalty tests

hobbies-respected.prompt: Personal hobbies and interests get respect, even when not shared.

options.1: Personal hobbies feel like theft from the relationship
options.2: Allowed, but with teasing or "come home already" pressure
options.3: Partly respected — when they don't clash with plans
options.4: Each of us has an activity that gets steady space
options.5: Personal interests are honored — even when we don't share them

no-mind-reading.prompt: We don’t expect mind-reading — and we don’t take offense when someone asks for clarity.

options.1: We expect each other to know our thoughts without words
options.2: We ask "what's wrong?" and get offended that we have to explain
options.3: Sometimes we ask clearly; sometimes we sulk over not being guessed
options.4: If something's unclear, we ask — we don't guess or punish
options.5: No mind-reading — asking for clarity is closeness, not a flaw

boundaries-held.prompt: Boundaries we name are held, not erased two days later.

options.1: A boundary we set is gone within two days
options.2: We say "no" — then cave to keep the peace
options.3: Boundaries work in some areas, not others
options.4: What we agreed on holds even when family pushes
options.5: Named boundaries stay respected over time — not just on agreement day

togetherness-not-fusion.prompt: Our togetherness doesn’t require erasing who we are apart.

options.1: Being a couple means barely being separate people
options.2: One of us always adapts; the other less so
options.3: We have "us," but sometimes lose who we are alone
options.4: We're a strong "we" — and "I" and "you" still stand
options.5: Closeness without erasing who each of us is outside the couple

jealousy-handled.prompt: Jealousy or insecurity is handled in conversation, not through control.

options.1: Jealousy means phone checks, rules, or blowups
options.2: We swallow the feeling or explode without talking
options.3: We talk sometimes, but the worry doesn't fully settle
options.4: When insecurity flares, we open talk — not control
options.5: Jealousy stays in conversation — not in controlling each other

future-talks.prompt: We talk about the future honestly — dreams and fears alike.

options.1: The future is off-limits or only starts fights
options.2: We speak in generalities — not the real fears
options.3: We plan logistics more than dreams and deep worries
options.4: We share what scares us and what excites us about what's next
options.5: We talk about the future honestly — dreams and fears together

celebrate-wins.prompt: We celebrate each other even in small everyday wins.

options.1: One person's wins pass in silence — as if expected
options.2: We say "good job" mechanically and move on
options.3: Big wins get noticed; small daily ones don't
options.4: We mark each other's successes — even a good day at work
options.5: We celebrate each other out loud — including tiny everyday wins

learn-from-conflict.prompt: After conflict, something learned remains — not only a scratch.

options.1: After conflict only a shadow remains — nothing changes
options.2: We make peace, but the same issue returns again
options.3: Sometimes we learn; sometimes we just get tired
options.4: We leave a fight with a small rule or insight for next time
options.5: Something learned stays from each friction — not just a bruise

shared-rituals.prompt: We have small shared rituals (meal, walk, a show) that hold the bond.

options.1: We have no shared habit — only logistics
options.2: We used to — now everything gets postponed
options.3: A shared moment happens now and then, without rhythm
options.4: We keep a small fixed ritual — meal, walk, or a show
options.5: Shared rituals (food, walks, evenings) hold the bond in ordinary life

support-dreams.prompt: Each of us feels support for personal dreams — even when logistics are hard.

options.1: Personal dreams feel like a threat to the couple
options.2: Support is mostly words — logistics swallow the rest
options.3: We cheer when it's easy; when it's hard, we fade
options.4: We look for ways both the dream and home life can breathe
options.5: Each of us feels backed in personal dreams — even when it's messy

fair-load-home.prompt: Home load feels fair enough, and can be renegotiated.

options.1: Home load lands on one person — the other "helps" sometimes
options.2: We argue about who did more — with no clear split
options.3: The split is roughly even, but doesn't update when life shifts
options.4: We check who does what and rebalance when something's heavy
options.5: Home load feels fair enough — and we can renegotiate when needed

intimacy-of-ordinary.prompt: There’s intimacy between us in ordinary boredom — not only in peak moments.

options.1: Closeness only on "special" days — routine feels dry
options.2: We're side by side but rarely touch or connect
options.3: Warm moments in daily life happen, but they're rare
options.4: In boring Tuesdays there's touch, humor, or a look that feels like home
options.5: We feel close on gray days too — not only at the peaks
